text:
(2) In such a case the justice shall issue a summons directed to that person
requiring him to attend before a justice at the time and place appointed in
the summons to have his evidence taken as a deposition or to produce the
document or other exhibit.

(3) If a justice of the peace is satisfied by evidence on oath of the matters
mentioned in subsection (1) above, and also that it is probable that a
summons under subsection (2) above would not procure the result required
by it, the justice may instead of issuing a summons issue a warrant to arrest
the person concerned and bring him before a justice at the time and place
specified in the warrant.

(4) A summons may also be issued under subsection (2) above if the justice
is satisfied that the person concerned is outside the British Islands, but
no warrant may be issued under subsection (3) above unless the justice is
satisfied by evidence on oath that the person concerned is in England or
Wales.
